findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test file
findings.body: The PR introduces a brand new middleware file pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go containing the instrumentContext helper plus four RPC entry points (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) that propagate a contextual logger through the request context. No corresponding contextual_logger_middleware_test.go is added, so the behavior of instrumentContext (including the conditional dsName/dsUID/uname branches) and the context propagation through the middleware chain is entirely untested. The metrics_middleware_test.go rename only exercises the metrics side; nothing verifies that the new middleware actually enriches the context as advertised, or that the LoggerMiddleware downstream receives the expected attributes.

findings.title: Updated logRequest behavior is not covered by any test
findings.body: The logRequest method was reworked from passing an explicit logParams slice (with pluginId, endpoint, pluginCtx.User.Login, dsName, dsUID and traceID explicitly appended) and calling m.logger.Info(...) to instead calling m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) with a slimmed-down logParams. This is a meaningful behavioral change: the pluginId/endpoint/user/ds/traceID fields now come from the contextual logger rather than from explicit key/value pairs, which means the log payload silently loses those fields unless ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wired into the chain ahead of LoggerMiddleware. There is no test that verifies either the resulting log structure or the implicit ordering contract between these two middlewares, so a future reordering or refactor of CreateMiddlewares could regress the log output without any test failure.

findings.title: Test function name still references the old InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the only internal change is renaming newInstrumentationMiddleware to newMetricsMiddleware, but the top-level test function is still TestInstrumentationMiddleware. After the public type/constructor rename this name is misleading and makes the test harder to locate and reason about (it now looks like it tests a type that no longer exists). It should be TestMetricsMiddleware.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, breaking the standard TestLogger assertion pattern
findings.body: The newly added TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() (a brand-new TestLogger) instead of returning the receiver f. The LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now invokes m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that hands a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware (or any other component that calls FromContext on it) and then inspects the original instance's InfoLogs/WarnLogs/etc. will see zero calls because the log was recorded on a different TestLogger instance that the test never references. To keep the established pattern (pass a TestLogger, assert on its fields) TestLogger.FromContext should return f (or a thin wrapper that delegates to f) so assertions against the original instance still work.
